items.title: The Fock-space convention dictionary for finite type-A quantum modules
items.statement: Fix a nonempty set of consecutive integers $I$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)$, and let $U$ be the quantized enveloping algebra of $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ with generators $E_i,F_i,D_i^{\pm1}$ and comultiplication $\Delta(D_i^{\pm1})=D_i^{\pm1}\otimes D_i^{\pm1}$, $\Delta(E_i)=1\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$, $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+D_i^{-1}D_{i+1}\otimes F_i$, as in the Fock-space literature. This item freezes the exact dictionary between that presentation and the library conventions of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]] and [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]: the variable change $v\leftrightarrow q^{-1}$, the identification (in finite rank) of the $D_i$ with monomials in the library torus generators so that $D_iE_jD_i^{-1}=q^{(\epsilon_i,\alpha_j)}E_j$, the transport of Lusztig's coproduct to the library coproduct or its opposite exactly as fixed by the quantum-interface supplier, the bar involution $\bar q=q^{-1}$, $\bar E_i=E_i$, $\bar F_i=F_i$, $\bar D_i=D_i^{-1}$, and the identification of the natural module $V$ with the library integrable highest weight module of highest weight $\omega_1$, of the dual $V^*$ with that of highest weight $-\omega_n$, and of the fundamental modules with the quantum exterior powers below. All modules are weight modules with finite weight spaces, so the library based-module notions apply: the bar and integral lattices of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]], the Kashiwara lattices of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], the divided-power form of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and the contravariant form of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. No theorem is asserted: the item fixes the interface once, so that the Fock-space bar, integral forms and global bases below are quoted in the library normalization.
items.strategy: The dictionary is verified generator by generator against the library definitions: the Serre relations and triangular decomposition are the published quantum-Serre page and [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], the divided powers are [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], and existence/uniqueness of integrable highest weight modules is [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]. The comultiplication conventions are fixed by the owner quantum-interface direction (v=q^{-1}, unchanged divided generators, toral transport $K_h^L\mapsto K_{-h}$); the author must display the resulting identities rather than assert agreement of two differently normalized coproducts. Nothing else is proved here.

items.title: The higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module
items.statement: Fix $I$ consecutive, $\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+$ with $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ (level $l$, $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in the $j$-th column, $n=\sum_jn_j$). The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is $F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l})$, the tensor product of fundamental modules of the dictionary item; when $I$ is unbounded below each $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge $\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with basis the normally ordered wedges $v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$, $i_1>i_2>\cdots$, with $i_k=m_j+1-k$ for $k\gg0$. A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ (columns $1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$); it is **column-strict** if entries lie in $I^+$, strictly increase bottom to top in each column and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and **standard** if in addition entries weakly increase left to right in each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda,\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ for these sets, $A_\Lambda$ for the ground-state tableau (row $i$ filled with $i$), $M_A:=(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots)\otimes\cdots\otimes(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots)$ for the **column monomial**, $\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)}$, $\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A)$, and $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$ for $\alpha\in Q^+$. The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is $A\le B$ iff $\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and $\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$ in the dominance order for each $j<l$; then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$ in columns $i<j$. Column-reading compositions give the passage to partitions of [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and [[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]. The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is the unique monomial of weight $\Lambda$.
items.strategy: Definition only: the displayed assertions are definitions or immediate bookkeeping (bijectivity of reading down columns, one-dimensionality of the $\Lambda$-weight space of $F(\Lambda)$). The dominance/Bruhat comparison is [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]] with [[lem-conjugation-reverses-dominance]]; no freeness or basis statement is proved here. Weight bookkeeping uses [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]].

items.title: The column monomial basis of the higher-level Fock module
items.statement: In the notation of [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]: (1) (Finite wedges.) For bounded-below $I$ the normally ordered wedges $v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_k}$ ($i_1>\cdots>i_k$) form a basis of $\Lambda^kV$, the fundamental module $V(\Lambda_m)$ is $\Lambda^{m+1-\inf(I)}V$, and the column-strict one-column tableaux are its monomial labels. (2) (Truncations.) For $k\le m_l$ with $k-1\in I$ the embeddings $\iota_k:\Lambda^{m+1-k}V_{\ge k}\hookrightarrow\Lambda^{m+2-k}V_{\ge k-1}$, $v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_{m+1-k}}\mapsto v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_{m+1-k}}\wedge v_{k-1}$, tensor to embeddings of the truncated $F(\Lambda)^{\ge k}$, and the unbounded $F(\Lambda)$ is their direct limit. (3) (Basis.) The column monomials $\{M_A:A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda\}$ form a basis of $F(\Lambda)$: they are weight vectors of weight $\mathrm{wt}(A)$, distinct tableaux give independent vectors in the tensor product of wedge bases, and $\iota_k(M_A)=M_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$ for the row-extension $A\mapsto A\sqcup(k-1)^l$. (4) (Action.) The action of $U$ is well defined weightwise: each $F(\Lambda)_\mu$ is finite-dimensional and preserved by the generators, and the generator formulas act by finitely many terminating moves because only finitely many boxes of a column-strict tableau differ from the ground state.
items.strategy: Construction for bounded-below $I$: the quantum exterior powers are spanned by $v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_k}=\sum_{w\in S_k}(-q)^{\ell(w)}v_{i_{w(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{i_{w(k)}}$ for $i_1>\cdots>i_k$; their basis property is the triangularity of antisymmetrization against the monomial basis of the tensor power, and $V(\Lambda_m)=\Lambda^{m+1-\inf(I)}V$ is the bounded-below case of the source. The unbounded case is the truncation direct limit: the source's diagram (2.11)-(2.13) is the compatibility of monomials with the embeddings, and the direct limit carries the union of the monomial bases. Weightwise action is the tensor product rule ([[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]) plus weight finiteness of integrable modules ([[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]], [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]]). No dimension of any category-O Grothendieck group is used.

items.title: The tensor-product bar on the Fock module and its truncation compatibility
items.statement: Retain $F(\Lambda)$, its monomial basis and the dictionary item. (1) (Compatible bar.) $F(\Lambda)$ carries a unique $U$-compatible bar involution $\psi$ ($\psi(uv)=\bar u\,\psi(v)$) extending the bar that fixes every normally ordered wedge and is built from the quasi-$R$-matrix tensor construction; on every finite product of truncated fundamental factors it is the quasi-$R$-tensor bar supplied by [[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]], hence involutive, semilinear and independent of the parenthesization. (2) (Triangularity.) For every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, $\overline{M_A}=M_A+\bigl(\text{a }\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\text{-linear combination of }M_B\text{ with }B<A\bigr)$. (3) (Truncation compatibility.) $\psi(\iota_k(N))=\iota_k(\psi(N))$ for all $N$; consequently the direct limit carries a well-defined involutive compatible bar, whose restrictions are the truncated bars. (4) (Integral form.) $\psi$ preserves the integral lattice $F(\Lambda)_{\mathcal A}$ spanned by the monomials over $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$.
items.strategy: For each finite truncation the $l$ fundamental factors are finite-dimensional based integrable weight modules, so the field tensor-bar theorem of [[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]] applies to the finite product and gives an involutive, semilinear, $U$-compatible bar independent of parenthesization; the new content is the passage to the semi-infinite direct limit, which that theorem does not supply. This is proved exactly as the source's Lemma 2.1: the quasi-$R$-matrix of the truncated algebra $U_{\ge(k-1)}$ equals that of $U_{\ge k}$ plus terms annihilating vectors in the image of $\iota_k$ by weight considerations, so the two bars agree on $\iota_k(F(\Lambda)^{\ge k})$ and the truncated bars glue to a unique involution of the direct limit. Triangularity is read on the monomial basis: each correction replaces entries $i$ by $i+1$ in the wedge expansion, lowering the Bruhat order, with coefficients from the quasi-$R$-matrix. Integrality is [[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]] applied factorwise. The finite-product input is used only in its proved scope; no semi-infinite statement is imported from it.

items.title: The dual-canonical, canonical and quasi-canonical Fock bases
items.statement: Retain $F(\Lambda)$, its bar $\psi$ and the monomial basis; retain also the twisted module $\bar F(\Lambda)=V(\Lambda_{m_l})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_1})$ with the reverse-column monomial basis $\bar M_A$ (read down columns from the rightmost column), its bar and reverse crystal structure, $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ for the reverse-standard tableaux (reverse crystal component of the ground state), and the rectification bijections $A\mapsto A^\downarrow$, $A\mapsto A^\uparrow$ between $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$. The four bases of $F(\Lambda)$, all through $\psi$ and the pairings below: (i) the **monomial basis** $\{M_A\}_{A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda}$; (ii) the **dual-canonical basis** $\{L_A\}$, the unique $\psi$-fixed family with $L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}q\mathbb Z[q]M_B$; (iii) the **canonical basis** $\{T_A\}$, the unique $\psi$-fixed family with $T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}q^{-1}\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]M_B$, equivalently the $\psi$-fixed family dual to $\bar L_A$ under the contravariant form $(\bar M_A,M_B)=\delta_{A,B}$; (iv) the **quasi-canonical basis** $\{P_A\}$, defined by transposing transition matrices: $P_A=\sum_B d_{A,B}(q)M_B$ and $M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-q)P_B$, where $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(q)L_A$ and $L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-q)M_A$. The pairings are the sesquilinear form $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ (anti-linear in the first variable) with $\langle M_A,M_B\rangle=\delta_{A,B}$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{A,B}$, and the contravariant form $(\cdot,\cdot):\bar F(\Lambda)\times F(\Lambda)\to\mathbb Q(q)$ with $(\bar M_A,M_B)=\delta_{A,B}$ and $(\bar L_A,T_B)=\delta_{A,B}$. None is a synonym: $L_A=M_A$ only when the correction vanishes; $T_A$ and $P_A$ are generally not $\psi$-fixed; on the highest weight submodule the dual-canonical and canonical families are indexed by $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ respectively. The integral form $F(\Lambda)_{\mathcal A}$ of the preceding item is the $\mathcal A$-span of any of the four bases.
items.strategy: Definitions, with uniqueness supplied by the bar triangularity of [[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]] and the abstract bar/uniqueness results [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]; the pairing identities are checked by substituting the transition matrices and applying the bar to (2.17), as in the source. Well-definedness of the transition matrices uses unitriangularity from the triangular bar property; stability under the truncation embeddings makes all four definitions compatible with the direct limit. No equality between the four families is asserted; the distinctions are the subject of the companion example and counterexample items.

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials give the dual-canonical transition matrix
items.statement: Assume $I$ bounded below, so $n=\sum_jn_j<\infty$ and tableaux have finitely many entries. Retain the transition polynomials $p_{A,B}(q),d_{A,B}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]. (1) (Source formula.) For all $A,B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ with $A\le B$ in the Bruhat order, $$p_{A,B}(q)=q^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in Z_A}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,\,w_B}(q^{-2}),$$ where $w_A$ is the unique element of $S_n$ of minimal length such that the column reading of $A$ multiplied by $w_A$ is weakly increasing, $Z_A$ is the stabilizer of that weakly increasing sequence (a conjugate of the Young subgroup of the multiplicities of the column reading), and $P$ is the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial of [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]; the $p_{A,B}$ are Deodhar's parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials for the symmetric group, supported on $A\le B$ with $p_{A,A}=1$, and $d_{A,B}$ is the inverse-transpose family with the same support. (2) (Dictionary with the library families.) Under the explicit dictionary between $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, the minimal-length representatives $w_A$, the stabilizer $Z_A$ and the parabolic quotient $^JW$ of [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]], the matrix $(p_{A,B})$ coincides with the library family of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]: the antispherical (sign) family $N^J$ under the tableau-to-permutation dictionary identifying $Z_A$ with the parabolic subgroup $W_J$, and the spherical family $M^J$ under the finite-parabolic longest-element reduction $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ of [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]; the proof fixes the family and the index convention and verifies the match, it does not assume it. (3) (Value at one.) $d_{A,B}(1)=[M(B):L(A)]$ is the composition multiplicity in the corresponding parabolic block, under the block dictionary of [[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]], and it vanishes unless $A\le B$.
items.strategy: Part (1) is the source formula, reproduced with the source's identification of the $p_{A,B}$ as Deodhar's parabolic polynomials; the identity, support and unitriangularity are proved by expanding the $\psi$-invariant $L_B$ in the monomial basis and comparing with the two families (4.3) of the Hecke module $1_\lambda\otimes_{H_\lambda}H_d$, whose coefficients are the same parabolic polynomials. Part (2) is a normalization check and not an independent mathematical claim: the author must (a) match the source Hecke normalization ($H_i^2=1-(q-q^{-1})H_i$, $M_\lambda$ induced from the character $q^{-1}$) with the library normalization ($H_s^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_s$, $\underline H_s=H_s+v$); (b) match the index sets (column readings, minimal/maximal coset representatives, left versus right multiplication) using [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] and [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]; (c) verify the resulting identity in the two smallest nontrivial cases (the level-one $S_2$ block and the $S_3$ block with $J=\{s_1\}$), where both sides are computable from [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]. Part (3) is the categorification step: it follows from the block identification together with the independently proved singular-block multiplicity theorem, whose value at $q=1$ fixes the family; that comparison must be recorded. No positivity beyond $\mathbb Z[q]$ is asserted.

items.title: Standard tableau monomials form a basis of the highest weight Fock submodule
items.statement: Retain the notation of [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Since $v_\Lambda=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is a highest weight vector of weight $\Lambda$ and the $\Lambda$-weight space of $F(\Lambda)$ is one-dimensional, the submodule $V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$ generated by $v_\Lambda$ occurs with multiplicity one, and there is a canonical $U$-equivariant projection $\pi:F(\Lambda)\twoheadrightarrow V(\Lambda)$ onto the $V(\Lambda)$-isotypic component. Put $S_A:=\pi(M_A)$ and $D_A:=\pi(L_A)$. Then: (1) (Standard monomials.) $\{S_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is a basis of $V(\Lambda)$, $\pi(M_A)\ne0$ iff $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and $\{L_A:A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda\setminus\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is a basis of $\ker\pi$. (2) (Dual canonical restriction.) $\{D_A:A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is the dual-canonical (upper global) basis of $V(\Lambda)$ and $S_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(q)D_A$. (3) (Direct limit.) $\iota_k(S_A)=S_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$ and $\iota_k(D_A)=D_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$, so the unbounded standard monomial and dual-canonical bases are the unions of the bounded-below ones. This is a statement about the explicit monomial construction in the Fock module, not an inference from the dimension of any Grothendieck group or from the KL multiplicity theorem.
items.strategy: For bounded-below $I$ the standard monomial basis theorem is Theorem 26 of [[B1]]: the Littlewood-Richardson homomorphism $\xi_\mu$ sends dual-canonical basis elements to dual-canonical basis elements or zero, and the images of the standard monomials are the upper global crystal base of the irreducible representation; the base-change argument between balanced triples is in the source's proof. The library statement applies that theorem to the tensor product of the $l$ fundamental factors of $F(\Lambda)$; the projection $\pi$ is $\xi_\mu$ composed with the canonical identification of its image with the highest weight constituent (multiplicity one, [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]]). The vanishing criterion for $\pi(L_A)$ and the basis property are the source's Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 2.3. The unbounded case is the direct limit over truncations using the compatibility of $\pi$ with the embeddings (source diagram (2.11)) and (2.12)-(2.13). The library items [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]] and [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]] supply the abstract uniqueness and based-quotient language; no dimension count and no category-O input is used.

items.title: The integral parabolic category-O blocks for higher-level Schur-Weyl duality
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published category-O theory and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Fix $\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}$ with $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$ of level $l$, put $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$, $n=n_1+\cdots+n_l$ (so $\Lambda$ is the partition $(n_1,\dots,n_l)$ in $\varepsilon$-coordinates of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$), and let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l\oplus\mathfrak u$ be the standard parabolic of $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ with Levi factor $\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$, in the conventions of [[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]. Given $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ with column reading $a_1,\dots,a_n$, let $L(A)$ be the simple highest weight module of highest weight $a_1\varepsilon_1+(a_2+1)\varepsilon_2+\cdots+(a_n+n-1)\varepsilon_n$ (the weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ in the notation of [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]); each $L(A)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral, and $L(A)\cong L(B)$ iff $A=B$. For $\alpha\in Q^+$ let $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ with all composition factors among the $L(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, and let $\mathcal O^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$. Each non-zero $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ is a single block of the parabolic category and a highest weight category with standard objects $M(A)$ (generalized Verma modules), simples $L(A)$, projective covers $P(A)$ and costandard objects $\nabla(A)$, indexed by $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$; BGG reciprocity $(P(A):M(B))=[M(B):L(A)]$ and the standard/simple Grothendieck bases hold by [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]] and [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]. The duality of [[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]] restricts to an exact contravariant involution with $L(A)^\star\cong L(A)$, $M(A)^\star\cong\nabla(A)$. Passing from $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ to $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\beta$ shifts the central character from $\Lambda-\alpha$ to $\Lambda-\beta$.

The obligation of the item is that the indexing conventions (columns of $\Lambda$, column readings, $\varepsilon$-coordinates) are displayed so that later multiplicity statements have exact indices. The Axiom of Choice is inherited and declared; no new choice principle is introduced.

items.title: The residue translation functors on the sum of parabolic blocks
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and retain the blocks $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$. Let $V$ be the natural $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-module and $V^*$ its dual. For $i\in I$ define $$f_i:\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathcal O^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\quad f_i(M):=\mathrm{pr}_{\alpha+\alpha_i}(M\otimes V),\qquad e_i:\mathcal O^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}\to\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha,\quad e_i(M):=\mathrm{pr}_\alpha(M\otimes V^*),$$ the projection onto the block of central character $\Lambda-\alpha-\alpha_i$ (equivalently the generalized $i$-eigencomponent of the Casimir-compatible endomorphism, in the conventions of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]); taking the direct sum over $\alpha$ gives exact endofunctors $e_i,f_i$ of $\mathcal O^\Lambda$. They are biadjoint, hence exact, commute with the duality $\star$, preserve finite-length objects and send projectives to projectives. The block shift is $\alpha\mapsto\alpha\pm\alpha_i$. These are the residue translation functors attached to the residue $i$; they are the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-type wall-crossing translation functors of [[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] transported through the block data. Finally $\mathcal O^\Lambda=\bigoplus_\alpha\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the decomposition into generalized central-character blocks of [[thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character]].
items.strategy: Definitions and standard properties: $\mathrm{pr}$ is the idempotent endofunctor onto one block of the direct sum decomposition, exact by [[thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character]]; tensoring with a finite-dimensional module is exact and preserves projectives ([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]], [[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]); biadjunction and exactness are [[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] applied wall by wall. The only content is the correct indexing of blocks and the explicit statement that $f_i$ raises and $e_i$ lowers the block label, with $\star$-compatibility checked directly on tensoring with a self-dual or dual module. The Axiom of Choice is inherited.

items.title: The residue translation functors give the integrable Fock-space action
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and retain the preceding notation; let $U_{\mathbb Z}$ be the Kostant $\mathbb Z$-form of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$ with Chevalley generators $e_i,f_i$, $i\in I$. Then: (1) (Standard flags.) For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, the modules $f_iM(A)$ and $e_iM(A)$ have multiplicity-free generalized Verma flags with sections $M(B)$ for the tableaux $B$ obtained from $A$ by replacing one entry $i$ by $i+1$ (for $f_i$), respectively one entry $i+1$ by $i$ (for $e_i$). (2) (Operators.) The induced operators on the Grothendieck group satisfy the Chevalley and Serre relations of $U_{\mathbb Z}$ in the block decomposition of the Fock space, with $[f_i],[e_i]$ matching the generators: this is verified on the generalized Verma flag sections (the monomial basis) and extended by linearity; an action on labels alone is insufficient and is not used. (3) (Crystal.) On irreducible classes, $e_iL(A)
e0$ (resp. $f_iL(A)
e0$) iff the crystal operator $	ilde e_i(A)
e\varnothing$ (resp. $	ilde f_i(A)
e\varnothing$), and then $e_iL(A),f_iL(A)$ are self-dual indecomposables with socle and head $L(	ilde e_iA)$, $L(	ilde f_iA)$; the label combinatorics is the crystal $(\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda,	ilde e_i,	ilde f_i,\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i,\mathrm{wt})$ of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]] and [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]], and the functor action matches [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]]. (4) (Integrability and highest vector.) The $U_{\mathbb Z}$-module generated by the class of $M(A_\Lambda)$ has finite-dimensional weight spaces $F(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z,\Lambda-\alpha}$ with one basis vector per $\Lambda$-tableau of weight $\Lambda-\alpha$, hence is integrable, and $M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$ is a highest weight vector of weight $\Lambda$.

Part (2) is checked on the standard classes: $[f_i],[e_i]$ act on monomials by the finitely supported moves of part (1); the Serre relations are verified coefficientwise in that basis and extended by linearity, and $[e_i,f_j]=\delta_{ij}h_j$ is read off from the block shifts. Part (3) is the source's crystal description [BK3, Theorem 4.5], cited as an additional input, not inferred. Part (4) is the weight finiteness of [[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]] plus one-dimensionality of the $\Lambda$-weight space; integrability in the sense of [[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]] follows since weight multiplicities are finite and the crystal is a union of highest weight components. No action on labels alone is used.

items.title: The parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Retain $\mathcal O^\Lambda=\bigoplus_\alpha\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ and $F(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$. (1) (Standards to monomials.) The assignment $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, extends uniquely to an isomorphism of abelian groups $[\mathcal O^\Lambda]=\bigoplus_{\alpha}K_0(\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$, because both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules on the standard and monomial classes and the weight degrees match ($\deg[M(A)]=\Lambda-\mathrm{wt}(A)$). (2) (Functoriality.) Under this isomorphism the operators induced by $e_i,f_i$ are exactly the Chevalley operators of the integrable $U_{\mathbb Z}$-module $F(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], so the isomorphism is an isomorphism of $U_{\mathbb Z}$-modules. (3) (Pairing.) For every projective $P$ and every object $N$ of $\mathcal O^\Lambda$, $\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$, where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the Fock form of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] at $q=1$; in particular $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{A,B}$ matches $\dim\mathrm{Hom}(P(B),L(A))=\delta_{A,B}$, in agreement with BGG reciprocity.
items.strategy: The standard classes form a basis by BGG reciprocity and [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]], [[thm-finite-length-grothendieck-groups-have-simple-class-bases]]; freeness is block finiteness. Part (2) is [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] transported through the basis identification, and is the point where the operator identities must be checked on the standard (flag) basis, not read off from labels. Part (3) is the source pairing statement: the Fock form is defined by $\langle M_A,M_B\rangle=\delta_{A,B}$ with functoriality $\langle ux,y\rangle=\langle x,\tau(u)y\rangle$ for the appropriate anti-automorphism; at $q=1$ it is the projective/simple Hom pairing because $\dim\mathrm{Hom}(P(A),L(B))=\delta_{A,B}$ and both sides are additive over the block decomposition. The comparison with BGG reciprocity uses [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]. No identification of $[L(A)]$ or $[P(A)]$ with the dual-canonical or quasi-canonical basis is made here; that is the later basis-dictionary theorem.

items.title: Standard- and costandard-filtered objects and tilting objects
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be one of the blocks $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ (or more generally a finite highest weight category: abelian of finite length with a finite poset of simples, standard objects $\Delta(\lambda)$, costandard objects $
abla(\lambda)=\Delta(\lambda)^\star$, projectives standard-filtered, injectives costandard-filtered, and $\mathrm{Ext}^i_{\mathcal C}(\Delta(\lambda),
abla(\mu))=0$ for $i>0$). Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ for the full subcategory of objects with a finite filtration whose subquotients are standards (**standard filtration**, or Verma flag) and $\mathcal F(
abla)$ for the analogous **costandard filtration**. An object $T$ is **tilting** if $T\in\mathcal F(\Delta)\cap\mathcal F(
abla)$; it is a **partial tilting** with respect to a down-set $\Gamma$ if the standard filtration uses only labels in $\Gamma$. Recorded standard facts: $\mathcal F(\Delta),\mathcal F(
abla)$ are closed under direct sums and direct summands; the standard multiplicity $(T:\Delta(\lambda))$ is independent of the flag; $\dim\mathrm{Hom}(\Delta(\lambda),
abla(\mu))=\delta_{\lambda\mu}$ and higher Ext vanishes; $\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\mathrm{Ext}^i(N,
abla(\lambda))=0\  orall i>0,\lambda\}$. Duality $\star$ exchanges the two filtered categories and fixes tilting objects up to isomorphism. The **highest weight support condition** used for uniqueness is: if an indecomposable tilting $T$ has $\Delta(\lambda)$ among its standard sections, then in every standard flag the section of minimal occurring label is unique and occurs at the bottom and all other sections have strictly larger label; this is the order-theoretic input for peeling off the bottom section.
items.strategy: Definitions with standard facts quoted from published items: finite length, projective Verma flags, injective costandard flags, Hom/Ext vanishing and duality are [[thm-every-category-o-object-has-finite-length]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], [[cor-injectives-have-costandard-filtrations]], [[lem-standard-costandard-hom-and-ext-vanishing]] and [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]; BGG reciprocity and its consequences are [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]. The support condition is the peeling statement of [[lem-maximal-weight-verma-peels-off-a-standard-filtration]]. No existence of tilting objects is asserted here.

items.title: Indecomposable tilting objects exist and are classified in parabolic category O
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ be a non-zero parabolic block with labels $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$ ordered by the Bruhat order. Then: (1) (Existence and uniqueness.) For every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$ there is a unique up to isomorphism indecomposable $T(A)\in\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ in $\mathcal F(\Delta)\cap\mathcal F(\nabla)$ whose standard flag starts with $\Delta(A)$ at the bottom and has all other sections of strictly larger label; equivalently $\mathrm{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O}(\Delta(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$ and some standard flag of $T(A)$ starts with $\Delta(A)$. (2) (Classification.) Every tilting object of $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ is a direct sum of copies of the $T(A)$; in particular $[T(A)]$ is a basis element of the Grothendieck group. (3) (Partial tiltings.) For every down-set $\Gamma$ and $A\in\Gamma$ there is a unique indecomposable partial tilting $T_\Gamma(A)$ with standard flag using only labels in $\Gamma$ and starting with $\Delta(A)$; the system is nested with standard-filtered cokernels and its direct limit is $T(A)$. (4) (Duality.) $T(A)^\star\cong T(A)$.
items.strategy: The construction is the Ringel-Soergel successive-universal-extension argument as proved in [[BTS]] Theorem 5.1 (existence of the partial tiltings $T_{\ge n}(E)$ with the bottom-section property, the nesting inclusions and the direct limit) and Theorem 6.3 (the ungraded statement), with Example 7.1 identifying the classical case with BGG category O; the finiteness hypotheses (A7)-(A8) hold because each block has finitely many simples and enough projectives and injectives ([[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]], [[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]]). Uniqueness is the bottom-section argument: for two such tiltings the Hom space is controlled by the common bottom section ([[lem-standard-costandard-hom-and-ext-vanishing]], [[lem-maximal-weight-verma-peels-off-a-standard-filtration]]), and self-duality plus indecomposability force the identity. Part (2): a direct summand of a tilting is tilting by [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]; it has a bottom section $\Delta(A)$ and is isomorphic to $T(A)$ by uniqueness; decomposition into indecomposables is [[lem-finite-length-objects-decompose-into-indecomposables]]. Part (4) follows since the dual of a tilting with bottom section $\Delta(A)$ is again a tilting with the same bottom section. The Axiom of Choice is inherited.

items.title: The Ringel dual of a finite highest weight ideal
items.statement: Retain a finite parabolic block $\mathcal C=\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ with indecomposable tiltings $T(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$. (1) The **characteristic tilting object** $T_{\mathcal C}:=\bigoplus_AT(A)$ is a full tilting generator (every tilting lies in $\mathrm{add}\,T_{\mathcal C}$), is Ext-self-orthogonal and has finite projective dimension. (2) The **Ringel dual** of $\mathcal C$ is the algebra $R_{\mathcal C}:=\mathrm{End}_{\mathcal C}(T_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $R_{\mathcal C}\text{-mod}$ is a highest weight category whose standard objects are the images under $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T_{\mathcal C},-)$ of the *costandard* objects of $\mathcal C$, with the **reversed poset**: the indecomposable projectives of $R_{\mathcal C}\text{-mod}$ correspond to the tiltings $T(A)$ of $\mathcal C$. (3) The functor $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T_{\mathcal C},-)$ is fully faithful on $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ and identifies it with the costandard-filtered objects of the Ringel dual; dually the Hom functor from the projective generator $M_{\mathcal C}=\bigoplus_AP(A)$ identifies $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ with the standard-filtered objects of $\mathcal C$. Only the abstract construction and the reversed-poset bookkeeping are fixed here; the identification with a category of parabolic modules is the next item.

The obligation of the item is the correct reversal of the poset and the explicit correspondence projectives of the Ringel dual $\leftrightarrow$ tiltings of $\mathcal C$.

items.title: Type-A parabolic category-O Ringel duality via the opposite parabolic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Retain $\Lambda$, $\mathfrak p$ with Levi $\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$, $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, and let $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ be the opposite parabolic (Levi blocks in the reverse order), with category $\bar{\mathcal O}^\Lambda$ and objects $\bar M(A),\bar L(A),\bar P(A)$ indexed by the same set $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ via the reverse column reading. Let $S_\gamma$ be the semi-regular $(U(\mathfrak g),U(\mathfrak g))$-bimodule attached to an admissible semi-infinite character $\gamma$ and put $\mathbb T(M):=(S_\gamma\otimes_{U(\mathfrak g)}M)^\star$. Then: (1) (Standard/costandard transport.) $\mathbb T$ restricts to an exact contravariant equivalence between the standard-filtered objects of $\bar{\mathcal O}^\Lambda$ and the costandard-filtered objects of $\mathcal O^\Lambda$, with $\mathbb T(\bar M(A))\cong M(A)^\star=\nabla(A)$ up to the explicit labelling shift $A\mapsto C_{-\gamma}\otimes A^{\#}$ (the identity on labels for the type-A parabolic data in the standard normalization). (2) (Projectives to tiltings.) $\mathbb T(\bar P(A))\cong T(A)$; hence the Ringel dual of the block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the opposite-parabolic block $\bar{\mathcal O}^\Lambda_\alpha$. (3) (Reciprocity.) For all $A,B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, $(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$. (4) (Blocks.) The equivalence is compatible with the block decompositions and with finite down-set ideals, and restricts to each finite ideal and each single block.
items.strategy: The engine is the semi-regular bimodule construction, proved in full in the source: Lemma 5.3 constructs $S_\gamma=U(\mathfrak n)^{\circledast}\otimes_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak b)$ and verifies its bimodule properties; Theorem 5.4 proves that $M\mapsto S_\gamma\otimes_{U(\mathfrak g)}M$ and $N\mapsto\mathrm{Hom}_{U(\mathfrak g)}(S_\gamma,N)$ are mutually inverse equivalences between the free and cofree categories preserving short exact sequences; Corollary 5.7 and Theorem 6.4 give the contravariant equivalence of $\Delta$-filtered categories with $\Delta(E)\mapsto\Delta(C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^{\#})$ and $P\mapsto T$; Corollary 5.8 and (6.5) give $(T(E):\Delta(F))=[\nabla(C_{-\gamma}\otimes F^{\#}):L(C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^{\#})]$, proved from Corollary 5.7 and BGG reciprocity; Example 7.1 identifies the classical case with BGG category O. The two parabolics are interchanged by conjugation by the longest element $w_0$ of $S_n$. The step that must be carried out explicitly here is the type-A parabolic refinement: the restriction of the equivalence to the $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite categories and the identification of the labelling shift with the reverse-column reading; the accessible source version is stated for the Borel case, so the author must verify the dictionary $E\leftrightarrow C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^{\#}$ on type-A labels, check the standard/costandard transport on the smallest parabolic block, and then extend by the directed union over finite ideals. Do not assume the parabolic statement from the Borel statement; prove the refinement, or report the exact remaining gap. The Andersen-Stroppel twisting-functor interface (definition via $S_w$, right exactness, block preservation, commutation with finite tensoring and translation functors, acyclicity on Verma-flagged objects, action on dual Vermas, derived auto-equivalence) must be reconciled with this bimodule convention.

items.title: Simples, projectives and tiltings map to the three distinguished Fock bases
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, work in a block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ with the identification $[\mathcal O^\Lambda]\cong F(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ of [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]], and retain the four Fock bases of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]. Then for every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$: (1) $[L(A)]=L_A$, the dual-canonical basis element; (2) $[P(A)]=P_A$, the quasi-canonical basis element; (3) $[T(A)]=T_A$, the canonical basis element, computed by the twisted transition matrix $\bar d_{A,B}(1)$ (Arkhipov-Soergel reciprocity). Equivalently: the matrix of standard multiplicities of the indecomposable tiltings is the inverse-transpose of the matrix of composition multiplicities of the simples, and the three families of indecomposable objects are the three distinguished Fock bases. Everything is at $q=1$: the bases are specializations of the Fock bases, not graded lifts of the modules.
items.strategy: Part (1): $[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ by the parabolic multiplicity theorem [[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] transported through the block dictionary of [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]]; inverting the unitriangular matrix and using the defining bar/triangularity property of $L_A$ gives $[L(A)]=L_A$. Part (2): BGG reciprocity $(P(A):M(B))=[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ and $P_A=\sum_Bd_{A,B}(q)M_B$ at $q=1$ give $[P(A)]=P_A$. Part (3): Arkhipov-Soergel reciprocity of [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]] identifies the standard multiplicities of $T(A)$ with the composition multiplicities of the opposite parabolic, whose transition matrix is the twisted one; the canonical basis is characterized by the corresponding bar/triangularity, so substituting into $[T(A)]=\sum_B(T(A):M(B))M_B$ gives $T_A$. The equalities are in the Grothendieck group; no identification of upper with lower global bases and no grading on category O is asserted.

items.title: The Fock pairing matches the projective-simple and standard-costandard pairings
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; retain the Fock pairings of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and the categorification of [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]. (1) (Projective-simple.) For $A,B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{A,B}=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P(A),L(B))$, and more generally $\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ for projective $P$; thus the Fock sesquilinear form at $q=1$ is the projective-simple Hom pairing of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]. (2) (Standard-costandard.) The contravariant form $(\cdot,\cdot)$ restricts on $V(\Lambda)$ to the Shapovalov form and satisfies $(\bar L_A,T_B)=\delta_{A,B}$; at $q=1$ it matches the standard-costandard pairing $\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(M(A),\nabla(B))=\delta_{A,B}$ of [[lem-standard-costandard-hom-and-ext-vanishing]], the costandard factor being identified through the exact contravariant duality $\star$ of [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]. (3) (Normalizations.) The sesquilinear form is anti-linear in the first variable and semilinear for $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, its monomial bases are orthonormal, and its restriction to the highest weight submodule is the Shapovalov form of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]; the bilinear contravariant form pairs the twisted module $\bar F(\Lambda)$ with $F(\Lambda)$. The two pairings are not the same form: $(\bar L_A,T_B)=\delta_{A,B}$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{A,B}$ involve different bases and different modules, and neither implies an identification of upper with lower global bases.
items.strategy: Part (1) is the source's Theorem 3.1(ii) together with $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{A,B}$ from the transition matrices; the Hom pairing and its additivity are [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]] and [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]. Part (2) is the source's Lemma 2.6 (comparison of the Shapovalov and contravariant forms) together with the identification of the $q=1$ forms with the Hom pairing via duality; the costandard side uses $M(A)^\star\cong\nabla(A)$ and Hom/Ext vanishing. Part (3) is bookkeeping: the author must display the semilinearity of each form, the modules on which it is defined, and the exact pairing statements, and must not identify $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ with $(\cdot,\cdot)$ or $\bar F(\Lambda)$ with $F(\Lambda)$.

items.title: The highest weight Fock submodule carries the quantum-group global bases
items.statement: Retain $F(\Lambda)$, its bar $\psi$, the projection $\pi:F(\Lambda)\twoheadrightarrow V(\Lambda)$ and the library global bases of $V(\Lambda)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]] and [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]] (through the convention dictionary of the first item). Then: (1) the Fock dual-canonical basis restricts to the upper global basis of $V(\Lambda)$: $D_A=\pi(L_A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed element of the costandard form $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathcal A}$ with $D_A=S_A+\sum_Bq\mathbb Z[q]S_B$; (2) the Fock canonical basis restricts to the lower global basis after the explicit power normalization: $P_A=q^{\frac12(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)}T_{A^\uparrow}$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$, so the family $\{T_{A^\uparrow}\}$ (after removing that scalar $q$-power) is the lower global basis of the standard form $V(\Lambda)_{\mathcal A}$; (3) consequently the KL-defined Fock bases and the library's Kashiwara-Lusztig global bases coincide on $V(\Lambda)$ under the explicit bar/normalization dictionary, hence also after the specializations of [[prop-global-bases-specialize-to-integral-weight-bases]]. The comparison is by the characterizing properties (bar invariance, triangularity with respect to the monomial/standard bases, and duality under the pairings), not by an identification of constructions.
items.strategy: Uniqueness method: the library lower and upper global bases are characterized by bar invariance, triangularity and pairing duality ([[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]), while the Fock bases $L_A,T_A$ are bar-invariant with the corresponding triangularities by [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]]. It therefore suffices to (a) verify that the truncated Fock factors meet the hypotheses of the library's based-module/global-basis machinery (finite ordered products of based integrable modules, the scope explicitly proved on the balanced-triples page) using [[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]]; (b) identify the two normalizations of the canonical basis by the explicit power of the source's Theorem 2.7; and (c) use the pairing duality of the previous item. No identification of upper with lower global bases and no graded or root-of-unity claim beyond [[prop-global-bases-specialize-to-integral-weight-bases]] is allowed.

items.title: Residue translation on small parabolic category-O standards
items.statement: Take the smallest case in which the residue functors move a standard: $I=\{0,1\}$, $\Lambda=\Lambda_0+\Lambda_0$, so $F(\Lambda)=V\otimes V$ with monomials $M_{ab}$ and the two residue operators $f_0,e_0,f_1,e_1$. Give the explicit actions: (1) $f_iM_{ab}$ and $e_iM_{ab}$ as $\mathbb Z$-linear combinations of standard classes (multiplicity-free, by replacing one entry $i$ by $i+1$, respectively $i+1$ by $i$); (2) the corresponding Chevalley relation on this four-dimensional space, e.g. $[e_i,f_i]$ acting by the Cartan generator on the weight spaces and $[e_i,f_j]=0$ for $i\ne j$; (3) the crystal operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on the four tableaux and the matching with the functor action on irreducible classes; (4) the vacuous/vanishing cases (a replacement that would leave $I^+$ or produce a non-column-strict tableau gives zero). The example is the level-two rank-two instance of the categorification and must be computed in the standard (generalized Verma) basis, not by listing labels alone.
items.strategy: Finite computation: the moves are the source's Lemma 4.3 specialization to the two-box columns; the Chevalley relations are checked by applying both sides to each of the four standard classes and comparing in the Fock module [[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]]; the crystal actions are the combinatorial operators on the four tableaux. BGG reciprocity and the flag bookkeeping are used only to interpret the computed classes, per [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the category-O items.

items.title: Opposite-parabolic Ringel duality on a finite ideal
items.statement: Take the smallest type-A parabolic block with a non-trivial opposite: $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_3$, $\Lambda=(2,1)$ (so $\mathfrak p$ has Levi $\mathfrak{gl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_1$ and $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ the opposite), and restrict to a finite down-set ideal of the label poset containing at least two comparable labels. Exhibit: (1) the standard and costandard objects of the opposite-parabolic block on the chosen ideal; (2) the image of the twisting duality $\mathbb T$ on each standard and each projective of the ideal, verifying $\mathbb T(\bar M(A))\cong\nabla(A)$ and $\mathbb T(\bar P(A))\cong T(A)$ on the ideal; (3) the resulting reciprocity matrix $(T(A):M(B))$ and its identification with the opposite-parabolic composition matrix $[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$, computed from the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig data of the block; (4) the induced identification of the three Fock bases with simples, projectives and tiltings on this ideal. The example must be computed from the frozen conventions of the definition items, not by citing the general theorem alone.
items.strategy: Finite computation: the standard/costandard labels of the two parabolics are matched by the reverse-column reading; the twisting duality is applied through the explicit construction of [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]] (semi-regular bimodule), and the multiplicity matrices are computed from the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials on the ideal. The author must record the labelling dictionary explicitly and verify that the computed reciprocity matrix equals the opposite-parabolic composition matrix entrywise on the ideal; the general theorem then identifies the bases. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the category-O items.

items.title: The canonical and quasi-canonical bases need not coincide
items.statement: There is no identity between the canonical and quasi-canonical bases of the Fock space: they are different families, indexed by the same set but with different transition matrices relative to the monomial basis, and on the highest weight submodule $V(\Lambda)$ the quasi-canonical basis element $P_A$ of weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ equals $q^{\frac12(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)}T_{A^\uparrow}$ with $A^\uparrow\in\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$, so whenever $A^\uparrow\ne A$ and $\frac12(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)>0$ the two basis elements differ by a non-trivial monomial factor and are not equal as elements of $F(\Lambda)$, nor are their index-dependent transition matrices the same. Concretely, in the two-factor example (or any case with a non-trivial interval $A<A^\uparrow$), the coefficient $d_{A,A^\uparrow}(q)=q^{a}$ with $a=\frac12(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)$ is a non-constant monomial between distinct labels, so the canonical and quasi-canonical families differ from the dual-canonical family and from each other; in particular they cannot be substituted for one another in the categorification, where tiltings correspond to the canonical and projectives to the quasi-canonical basis. The counterexample does not claim that the bases differ at $q=1$ for every label: it exhibits the non-trivial monomial factor and the resulting non-equality of the two families.
items.strategy: Compute on the smallest case with $A^\uparrow\ne A$: the source's Corollary 2.8 gives $d_{A,A^\uparrow}(q)=q^{a}$ and $d_{A,A}(q)=1$ with $a=\frac12(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)>0$, and Theorem 2.7 gives $P_A=q^aT_{A^\uparrow}$; substituting into the definitions of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] yields two different bases. The author must exhibit the explicit pair/label, compute both transitions, and check that the difference survives (the monomial factor is not a scalar of the form $q^b$ with $b=0$). The statement is a non-coincidence statement and does not contradict the equality of the two families after the identification of the index sets $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\leftrightarrow\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$; that identification is exactly what must not be conflated with an equality of bases.
